input: When it comes to selectivity, the two studies of the benchmark material do not agree with one another, and the disagreement lies in the values that each reports for the same class of material rather than in the materials being compared. The first study measured mixture uptake directly, at the feed composition and pressure of the separation this review covers, and its selectivities are ratios of adsorbed amounts taken from those mixture measurements. The second study, by contrast, measured single-component isotherms and obtained its selectivities from IAST, so that its values inherit every assumption the theory makes about the adsorbed phase, including the mixing behaviour the isotherms are fitted to. When the two sets of values are placed side by side, the mixture values turn out to be the lower of the two, and the gap between the two sets widens as the feed moves away from the composition at which the isotherms were measured. The preference here is for the mixture measurements, on the condition that holds throughout this section: the material is being ranked for the stated separation, at the stated feed, and a value measured on that feed answers the ranking question without an intervening model. The preference is, however, limited to that use. For compositions the second study did not measure, its values are the only values available, and they enter the comparison with the model step stated.
